task.description: Independent design-gate review of lib/letflow/design/iss0437-admission-tenant-eviction.md against docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md Step 1b.

result.note:
FAIL -- genuine unaddressed correctness defect in the in-use eviction race (design §2/§4), found by independent trace-through, not by trusting the design's own race analysis.

What checks OUT (confirmed independently, not from the handoffs' prose): (1) grep for defmodule/def /defp /schema "/Enum\./fn ->/case do/cond do/with do/|> over the entire design doc returned ZERO matches -- no disguised executable code, only prose/@spec/@type. (2) lib/letflow/admission.ex read directly: state.tenants genuinely never evicts (only try_acquire/release/reserved_headroom/global_cap handle_call clauses exist, confirmed by reading init/1 through line 364); release_tenant/2's {:tenant, schema} clause (line 361-363) genuinely uses Map.update!/3, which raises KeyError on a missing key -- matches the design's claimed race exactly. ensure_tenant_tracked/2 (lines 347-353) genuinely does lazy Map.put(..., %{in_use: 0}) with no notion of 'previously forgotten' vs 'never seen' -- matches the design's reactivation claim. (3) Letflow.Identity.create_tenant/1 (lib/letflow/identity.ex:708-722) confirmed to NOT call TenantProvisioning itself -- its own @doc (lines 697-702) states the router orchestrates provisioning after create_tenant/1 returns, matching lib/letflow/routers/tenants.ex's provision_and_respond/2 (lines 253-260). The load-bearing precedent for keeping Admission wiring out of Identity.deactivate_tenant/1 holds up. (4) Letflow.Routers.Tenants.handle_deactivate/2 exists at lines 352-357 exactly as the design cites, and is the correct orchestration point. (7) Both doc-correction targets exist as described: admission.ex moduledoc section 'Lazy tenant-entry creation; no eviction (ISS-0437)' at lines 63-84 (second paragraph starting 'Entries are never evicted...' at line 72, matches verbatim), and req216-admission-control-core.md has a real §3 (line 242) and OQ-2 (line 467). (9) No changes to try_acquire/2's algorithm or unrelated routes found in the design text.

THE DEFECT (item 5 -- my own trace-through, independent of the design's claims): the design's §2 hardening of release_tenant/2 only distinguishes 'schema present in tenants' (decrement as today) vs 'schema absent' (no-op). This is insufficient once reactivation (§4) is considered together with eviction (§2) -- the two sections were reasoned about separately but not composed. Concrete sequence that produces a negative, out-of-bounds in_use count:
1. Tenant A active, two live refs ref1/ref2 both admitted, tenants["A"].in_use == 2.
2. Admin deactivates A -> Routers.Tenants calls forget_tenant("A") -> tenants["A"] deleted entirely (its in_use=2 knowledge discarded). refs map is untouched: refs still map ref1 and ref2 to {:tenant, "A"}.
3. Admin reactivates A before ref1/ref2 are released (plausible: no synchronization ties reactivation timing to in-flight request completion; TenantStatus only blocks NEW requests, per the design's own §2 admission).
4. A new request for A arrives; try_acquire({:tenant,"A"}) via ensure_tenant_tracked/2 creates a FRESH tenants["A"] = %{in_use: 0}, then admits it, giving in_use == 1 (ref3).
5. ref1 releases: schema "A" is now present again (from step 4) with in_use == 1 -> release_tenant/2 takes the 'present' branch and decrements to 0. No error, looks fine so far.
6. ref2 releases: schema "A" still present, in_use == 0 -> release_tenant/2 decrements 0 - 1 = -1. Map.update!/3 does not guard against going negative, and the design's proposed hardening does not either -- it only branches on key presence, not on which 'generation' of tracking the ref belongs to.

Consequence: tenants["A"].in_use becomes -1, violating the module's own declared type (%{in_use: non_neg_integer()} per the state-shape comment at admission.ex:246-255 and the design's own @spec for release_tenant/2 in §2). Worse than a crash: per_tenant_cap gating is `tenant_in_use < per_tenant_cap`, and a negative in_use always satisfies this, so tenant A silently gains extra, uncapped admission slots relative to every other tenant until enough NEW admissions bring its count back above 0 -- this is a NEW fairness bug (one tenant over-admitted) introduced by the fix for the ORIGINAL fairness bug (dilution), not a crash-safety gap. It is not a rare, contrived interleaving: deactivate-then-reactivate is exactly the administrative action pair this design's own §4 discusses, and the design nowhere requires or documents any minimum delay between them, nor any draining/quiescence guarantee before reactivation.

Why this must go back to CODE-DESIGNER rather than being waived: the design's §2 explicitly reasoned through 'release after eviction, no reactivation' (the KeyError-avoidance case) but never composed that with §4's reactivation scenario, despite both being in the same document and both concerning the same tenants map key. A key-presence check alone cannot distinguish 'this ref's tenant generation is still the one being tracked' from 'a same-named but logically distinct post-reactivation tracking session'. A fix needs either: (a) a generation/epoch tag stored per tracked entry (or per ref) so a stale release from a forgotten generation is recognized as stale even if the key has been recreated, or (b) clamping release_tenant/2's decrement at a floor of 0 (which prevents the negative excursion but silently under-counts the fresh entry's real in_use, potentially letting the reactivated tenant admit one more concurrent request than it should -- still a correctness compromise that needs to be reasoned through and stated, not left implicit), or (c) an explicitly reasoned argument for why this interleaving is impossible or out of scope, which the current design does not attempt.

Required rework: CODE-DESIGNER must revise §2 (and/or §4) of lib/letflow/design/iss0437-admission-tenant-eviction.md to address this composed race explicitly -- name the chosen mechanism, update release_tenant/2's @spec/behavior description accordingly, and add a fourth test (or extend Test 2 in §6) that specifically exercises deactivate -> reactivate -> stale-pre-eviction-release and asserts in_use never goes negative and never exceeds what a fresh reactivated tenant should be allowed.

All other checks (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9) passed independent verification. This is the sole reason for FAIL, but per workflow policy a single failed check fails the whole gate with no partial credit.
